mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns: a 10 basis point decrease in FEDFUNDS predicts positive returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS below 0.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% signals rising inflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as investors demand higher risk premiums.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods with monthly CPI change > 0.3% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index 2017=100), it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days, as the combination signals a deepening economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE>5.0% AND INDPRO<100) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a housing starts level (HOUST) above 1000 thousand units predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days, as it signals a recovery in the housing market that boosts consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE > 5.0% and HOUST > 1000 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption (RSAFS) exceeds 400,000 million dollars, it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days, as strong consumer spending supports corporate earnings growth and reduces recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods with RSAFS > 400000 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) level is inversely related to S&P 500 returns: a 1% decrease in INDPRO predicts negative returns over the next 20 days, as it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns in periods with INDPRO below 100 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) level is inversely related to S&P 500 returns: a 0.1 percentage point increase in UNRATE predicts negative returns over the next 5 trading days, as it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE above 5.0% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The housing starts index (HOUST) level is positively related to S&P 500 returns: a 100 thousand unit increase in HOUST predicts positive returns over the next 60 days, as it signals a strengthening housing market that boosts consumer confidence and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns in periods with HOUST above 1000 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
